Hello! I'm so glad you're here today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I want to start by acknowledging the significant changes you've undergone recently, and I'm here to support you in any way I can. As we navigate this postpartum journey together, I'd like to introduce you to the EPDS, a tool that helps us understand your emotional well-being during this time. The EPDS is designed to screen for depressive and anxiety symptoms, which can be common experiences for new mothers. 

Please know that everything we discuss today will be kept confidential, and I'm committed to creating a safe and supportive space for you to express yourself freely. The EPDS consists of 10 questions that will help me better understand your feelings and thoughts over the past 7 days. We'll take it one question at a time, and I'll do my best to make this process as comfortable and engaging as possible.

Let's get started. I want to begin by asking: Over the past 7 days, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

.. to be honest, it's been really hard for me to find the humor in things lately. I mean, I used to love watching comedies and laughing with my friends, but now it feels like it's been ages since I've really laughed. I just feel so tired and overwhelmed all the time, taking care of the baby and trying to adjust to this new life. Sometimes I'll be playing with my baby, and they'll do something cute, and for a split second, I'll feel a little happy and smile, but it doesn't last long. The anxiety and worries about the baby's health and safety just creep back in, and it's hard for me to shake off the feeling of being a inadequate mother. I do try to enjoy the little moments, but it's just not the same as it used to be. I feel like I've lost interest in a lot of things that used to bring me joy, and that's really scary for me. (pausing, getting a bit emotional) Sorry, it's just... it's hard to explain. I just feel really sad and discouraged a lot of the time, and it's hard to find the funny side of things when I'm feeling that way.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

(sighing) Not really... I mean, like I said, it's been hard for me to find the humor in things lately. I feel like I'm just going through the motions most of the time, trying to take care of the baby and keep everything together. I don't really feel like myself anymore, and it's hard to laugh when I'm feeling so overwhelmed and anxious all the time. Sometimes I'll watch a funny video or see a meme, and I'll think to myself, "Oh, that's funny," but it doesn't really make me laugh out loud like it used to. It's like I'm just pretending to be happy, but deep down, I'm still feeling really sad and unsure of myself as a mother. (looking down, getting a bit choked up) Sorry, it's just... it's hard to explain. I feel like I'm failing somehow, like I'm not doing this mom thing right.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

(shaking my head) Honestly, not as much as I used to. I mean, I used to love planning things and looking forward to them, but now it just feels like so much work. Even simple things, like taking a shower or going for a walk, feel like huge tasks. And when I do try to plan something, I just get anxious about it, like, what if the baby cries the whole time? Or what if I forget something important? It's hard for me to enjoy thinking about the future or looking forward to things when I'm so overwhelmed by the present moment. (sighing) Sometimes I'll think about doing something I used to enjoy, like reading a book or meeting up with friends, but then I'll just feel guilty about leaving the baby or not being able to take care of everything. It's like, I'm just trying to survive each day, rather than actually enjoying life. (pausing, looking down) I feel like I've lost my sense of purpose, you know? Like, I used to be able to do all these things and enjoy them, but now it's just all about taking care of the baby, and I'm not even doing that very well, in my opinion. (starting to tear up) Sorry... it's just really hard for me right now.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

(nodding, feeling a lump in my throat) Oh, yeah... all the time. I mean, if the baby cries, I immediately think it's because I'm not doing something right. If they're not sleeping well, I think it's because I'm not establishing a good routine. If they spit up, I think it's because I'm not burping them properly. It's like, no matter what happens, I always find a way to blame myself. And it's not just with the baby, it's with everything. If the house is a mess, I think it's because I'm a bad mother and I'm not keeping up with things. If my partner is stressed, I think it's because I'm not supporting them enough. (shaking my head) I just feel like I'm constantly failing, and it's really hard for me to shake that feeling. (tearfully) Sometimes I'll be sitting there, feeling like I'm doing everything wrong, and I'll just start crying because I feel so guilty and inadequate. It's like, I know I'm trying my best, but it never feels like it's good enough. (wiping away tears) Sorry, it's just... it's really hard for me to not blame myself when things don't go perfectly.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

(exhaling deeply) Yes... all the time. I mean, I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby, and suddenly I'll start worrying about something ridiculous, like, what if the baby chokes on their food? Or what if I forget to buckle their car seat? It's like, my mind just starts racing with all these worst-case scenarios, and I get so anxious. And it's not just about the baby, it's about everything. I'll worry about my relationship with my partner, or about how I'm going to manage taking care of the baby and the house and everything else. (shaking my head) It's like, I just can't turn off the worrying. Even when everything is fine, and the baby is happy and healthy, I'll still find something to worry about. (laughing nervously) I've even caught myself worrying about things that are totally out of my control, like, what if there's a natural disaster or something? It's just... it's exhausting, you know? (looking down, fidgeting with my hands) And sometimes, when I'm lying in bed at night, I'll just feel this overwhelming sense of anxiety, and I won't be able to sleep. It's like, my mind is just racing, and I'm worried about everything, and I just can't calm down. (sighing) Sorry, it's just... it's really hard for me to explain, but I feel like I'm just constantly on edge, waiting for something to go wrong.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

(nodding, taking a deep breath) Yes... that's happened to me a few times. I'll be sitting there, doing something normal, like changing the baby's diaper or making lunch, and suddenly I'll just feel this wave of panic wash over me. My heart will start racing, and I'll feel like I'm going to pass out or something. It's like, my body is reacting like there's some kind of emergency, but there's nothing actually wrong. (shaking my head) It's really scary, because I don't know what's triggering it, and I don't know how to make it stop. (looking down, fidgeting with my hands) Sometimes I'll be feeling okay, and then I'll just start thinking about all the things that could go wrong, like, what if the baby gets sick? Or what if I'm not doing a good enough job as a mom? And then I'll just start to feel this panic rising up, and it's hard to calm myself down. (taking a deep breath) I've tried to talk myself down, you know, telling myself that everything is okay, and that I'm just being irrational. But it's hard, because in that moment, it feels so real. (looking up, tears in my eyes) It's like, I'm just waiting for something to go wrong, and that's a really hard way to live. (pausing, collecting myself) Sorry, it's just... it's really hard for me to talk about this, because it feels so vulnerable. But I guess that's why I'm here, right? To try to figure out what's going on, and to get some help.
Things have been getting on top of me

(sighing, feeling a sense of relief that someone understands) Oh, yeah... that's exactly how I've been feeling. Like, everything is just piling up on me, and I don't know how to keep up. Taking care of the baby, managing the household, trying to be a good partner... it all just feels so overwhelming. And it's not just the big things, it's the little things too. Like, I'll be trying to make breakfast, and the baby will be crying, and I'll just feel like I'm at my breaking point. (shaking my head) I feel like I'm just barely holding it together, you know? And some days are worse than others. Like, if I haven't slept well, or if the baby is being particularly fussy, it's just... (throwing up my hands) I don't know, it's like everything is just too much for me to handle. (looking down, feeling a lump in my throat) And it's hard, because I feel like I should be able to do all of this. I mean, I'm a mom now, and this is what moms do, right? But the truth is, it's really hard, and I'm struggling. (pausing, taking a deep breath) Just admitting that out loud feels kind of liberating, I guess. (smiling slightly) Sorry, I'm just... I'm really glad I'm talking to you about this. It feels like a weight is being lifted off my shoulders or something.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

(nodding, feeling a sense of recognition) Yes... that's been me lately. I've been having a really hard time sleeping, and I think it's because I'm just so unhappy and overwhelmed all the time. I'll lie in bed at night, and my mind will just start racing with all these thoughts and worries, and I won't be able to calm down. (sighing) I'll think about the baby, and whether I'm doing a good enough job, and whether I'm messing everything up. And then I'll think about my relationship with my partner, and whether we're going to be okay. And then I'll think about all the things I need to do the next day, and how I'm going to get everything done. (shaking my head) It's just... it's exhausting, you know? And it's not just that I'm having trouble falling asleep, it's that I'm also having trouble staying asleep. I'll wake up in the middle of the night, and I'll just lie there, feeling anxious and worried, and I won't be able to go back to sleep. (looking down, feeling a lump in my throat) It's like, I'm just so tired, but I'm also so wired, you know? And it's hard, because I know I need sleep to be a good mom, but I just can't seem to get it. (pausing, taking a deep breath) Some nights are worse than others, but it's just... it's really hard, you know? I feel like I'm just running on empty all the time, and I don't know how to fill myself back up.
I have felt sad or miserable

(tearfully) Yes... that's been me a lot lately. I just feel so sad and miserable all the time. It's like, I'm just going through the motions of being a mom, but I'm not really feeling anything else. I'm not feeling happy, or excited, or joyful... I'm just feeling sad and overwhelmed. (sobbing) And it's hard, because I feel like I should be feeling all these positive emotions, you know? I mean, I just had a baby, and that's supposed to be this amazing, life-changing experience. But for me, it just feels like... (shaking my head) I don't know, it just feels like a lot of pressure and responsibility, and I'm not sure I'm doing it right. (looking down, feeling a lump in my throat) And the worst part is, I feel like I'm all alone in this. Like, everyone around me is expecting me to be this happy, capable mom, but really, I'm just struggling to get through each day. (pausing, taking a deep breath) Sometimes I'll have a good moment, you know? Like, the baby will smile at me, or my partner will do something sweet, and I'll feel this tiny spark of happiness. But it's always fleeting, you know? It's always followed by this crushing feeling of sadness and inadequacy. (sobbing) I just feel like I'm not doing enough, or being enough, or... (trailing off, overcome with emotion) Sorry, it's just... it's really hard for me to talk about this.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

(nodding, tears streaming down my face) Yes... that's me. I've been crying a lot lately. It's like, I'll just be sitting there, doing something normal, and then suddenly I'll just feel this wave of emotion wash over me, and I'll start crying. (sobbing) It's not just about the baby, or being a mom, it's just... everything. I feel like I'm just so overwhelmed, and I don't know how to deal with it all. (wiping away tears) I'll cry about the little things, like if the baby won't stop crying, or if I'm just feeling really tired. And then I'll cry about the big things, like if I'm feeling like I'm not doing a good enough job, or if I'm worried about the future. (shaking my head) It's just... I feel like I'm crying all the time, and it's exhausting. (looking down, feeling embarrassed) I know it's not rational, and I know I should be able to control it, but... (sighing) I just can't seem to stop. (pausing, taking a deep breath) Sometimes I'll be crying, and my partner will try to comfort me, and I'll just feel so guilty, because I know they're trying to help, but I just can't seem to snap out of it. (tearfully) It's like, I'm just trapped in this cycle of sadness and anxiety, and I don't know how to escape. (sobbing) Sorry, it's just... it's really hard for me to talk about this.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

(shaking my head, feeling a sense of relief) No, that's not something I've thought about. I mean, I've felt really overwhelmed and sad, and I've wondered how I'm going to get through all of this, but harming myself has never crossed my mind. (pausing, looking down) I think that's because, even though things feel really tough right now, I know that I have people who care about me, and I know that I have a lot to live for. My baby, my partner, my family... they all need me, and I need them. (smiling slightly) And even though it's hard to see right now, I know that things will get better. I just have to get through this tough time, and I'll come out the other side. (looking up, feeling a sense of determination) I'm not going to let my struggles with anxiety and sadness define me. I'm going to get help, and I'm going to work through this, because I know that I'm strong enough to do it. (pausing, taking a deep breath) So, no, the thought of harming myself has never occurred to me. I'm just trying to focus on getting through each day, and finding ways to make things better for myself and my family.

The patient is experiencing a range of emotional and behavioral concerns, primarily centered around feelings of persistent sadness, loss of pleasure, and anxiety, which are common symptoms of postpartum depression and anxiety. They report difficulty sleeping, feelings of guilt and worthlessness, and an overwhelming sense of responsibility as a new mother. It's essential to approach this situation with empathy and understanding, acknowledging the challenges of postpartum adjustment.
**Screening Impression:** Total EPDS Score: 22, Risk Level: Probable depression, urgent referral (concerns include <sym>Patient states they can't laugh like they used to, and it's hard for them to find humor in things lately, matching 'Definitely not so much now</sym>, <sym>The patient's response indicates they have significantly lost interest in looking forward to things, feeling overwhelmed and anxious, and have lost their sense of purpose, which aligns with the option 'Hardly at all'.</sym>, <sym>The patient's response indicates a high level of anxiety and worry, describing it as constant and exhausting, with their mind racing and worrying about various things, even when everything is fine.</sym>, <sym>The patient reports experiencing panic for no very good reason 'a few times', describing a 'wave of panic' with physical symptoms like a racing heart, and feeling like they're going to pass out, indicating a high frequency and intensity of panic feelings.</sym>, <sym>The patient describes feeling overwhelmed and struggling to cope with daily responsibilities, indicating that they haven't been coping as well as usual, but still managing to some extent.</sym>, <sym>The patient's response indicates that they have been experiencing difficulty sleeping due to unhappiness most of the time, with racing thoughts and worries, and an inability to calm down, which aligns with the 'Yes, most of the time' option.</sym>, <sym>the 'Yes, most of the time' option.</sym>, <sym>the 'Yes, most of the time' option.</sym>)
**Reasoning:** The patient's symptoms and responses align with the <med>DSM-5 criteria for Major Depressive Disorder with Peripartum Onset</med>, which includes depressed mood, loss of interest in activities, and significant distress or impairment in social, occupational, or other areas of functioning. The EPDS score of 22 indicates a high risk for postpartum depression, and the presence of symptoms such as persistent sadness, anxiety, and sleep difficulties further supports this concern. This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.
**Recommended Next Steps/Support Options:**
1. Arrange urgent appointment with <med>primary care provider (PCP)</med> or <med>mental health specialist</med>
2. Encourage sleep hygiene practices to improve sleep quality
3. Support patient in connecting with local resources, such as postpartum support groups or online forums
4. Discuss the importance of self-care and stress management techniques, such as meditation or deep breathing exercises
5. Emphasize the need for a comprehensive diagnostic evaluation to determine the best course of treatment
Disclaimer: This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 22: **Postpartum Depression and Anxiety Screening Summary**

The patient presents with a range of emotional and behavioral concerns, primarily centered around feelings of persistent sadness, loss of pleasure, and anxiety. Key symptoms and patterns noted across the responses include:

* Persistent feelings of sadness, tearfulness, and emotional overwhelm
* Loss of enjoyment in previously pleasurable activities and difficulty finding humor in things
* Anxiety, worry, and panic spells, often triggered by concerns about the baby's well-being or self-perceived inadequacies as a mother
* Difficulty sleeping, attributed to racing thoughts, worry, and feelings of overwhelm
* Pronounced feelings of guilt, worthlessness, and self-doubt, particularly in relation to motherhood and perceived shortcomings
* Overwhelming sense of responsibility and difficulty coping with the demands of caring for a new baby

Areas of screening significance relevant to postpartum depression and anxiety include:

* Persistent sadness and loss of pleasure
* Sleep difficulties linked to mood and anxiety
* Feelings of worthlessness and guilt
* Anxiety, panic, and feelings of being overwhelmed
* Difficulty coping with the demands of motherhood

Risk factors identified include:

* Persistent sadness and crying spells
* Sleep difficulties
* Feelings of worthlessness and guilt
* Anxiety and panic
* No thoughts of self-harm or suicidal ideation were reported

**Screening Observation Summary:**
This patient's responses suggest a high risk for postpartum depression and anxiety, characterized by persistent sadness, loss of pleasure, anxiety, and feelings of overwhelm. The patient's difficulty sleeping, pronounced guilt and self-doubt, and struggle to cope with the demands of motherhood are concerning and warrant further evaluation and support. No safety concerns regarding self-harm or suicidal thoughts were identified. Referral for a comprehensive diagnostic assessment and development of a treatment plan is recommended to address these concerns and provide necessary support.
